bibliographic.title: Automating financial compliance with AI: A New Era in regulatory technology (RegTech)
bibliographic.venue: International Journal of Science and Research Archive
bibliographic.citation_apa: Kothandapani, H. P. (2024). Automating financial compliance with AI: A New Era in regulatory technology (RegTech). International Journal of Science and Research Archive, 11(1), 2646-2659. https://doi.org/10.30574/ijsra.2024.11.1.0040

methodology.study_design: narrative literature review with case study discussion
methodology.sample_description: existing literature and case studies on AI in financial regulatory compliance
methodology.technology_context: RegTech; machine learning; natural language processing; predictive analytics; AML; sanctions compliance; fraud detection; generative AI mentioned as future trend

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article is a narrative review of AI in financial RegTech with governance, ethics, transparency, bias, and human oversight themes in a regulated domain. However, the provided text does not establish conversational AI, chatbots, agents, or LLM-based conversational systems as the study focus; LLMs and generative AI appear as cited literature or future trends rather than as the primary object of governance analysis.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Python triage flagged conversational terms not clearly supported in supplied excerpts; confirm whether chatbots or conversational governance appear elsewhere in the full PDF.

appraisal.notes: Abstract claims a comprehensive review of literature and case studies, but supplied text shows no explicit systematic search strategy, inclusion criteria, or reproducible review protocol. Suitable as contextual RegTech background, not as primary evidence on conversational LLM governance.

cerqual.explanation: For the review question on conversational governance of LLM systems in regulated settings, this paper offers only indirect relevance through general financial compliance governance and brief LLM/generative AI mentions; narrative review methods are weakly specified in the provided text.

axial_codes: AI automation in regulated financial compliance
coding.theme: AI-driven regulatory compliance in financial services
coding.subtheme: governance, ethics, and human oversight in RegTech

synthesis.main_claim: AI technologies, especially machine learning and NLP, can automate and improve financial regulatory compliance, while adoption requires addressing ethics, privacy, transparency, bias, and human oversight through robust governance frameworks.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a broad RegTech-oriented overview of AI applications in financial compliance and discusses governance and ethical challenges of deployment.
synthesis.limitations: Supplied text does not document systematic review methods, sampling, or primary empirical design; conversational AI and LLM governance are not central; LLM discussion appears secondary to broader AI compliance automation.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use only as borderline contextual evidence on general AI governance in regulated financial compliance; not suitable as central evidence for conversational LLM governance without further full-text verification.
